acceptance: musl and Windows arm64 wheel jobs generate TPC-H SF 0.01 tbl output and match the committed dbgen hashes.
A CI-built macOS arm64 wheel is shown to load and pass tests on macOS 27, or the failure is recorded with a minimal reproduction and an upstream report link.
Budget measurements for the library are re-run through the Python `write_tables` path on a host where release wheels load.
description:
## Problem
ADR decision 4 counts a platform as native only when data and query generation pass there. CI runs the full Python tests on Linux glibc (x86_64, aarch64), macOS (arm64, x86_64) and Windows x86_64, but only an import and PyCapsule check on musl (x86_64, aarch64) and Windows arm64, because pyarrow has no wheels there. Separately, on the maintainer's Mac (macOS 27 beta, ld 27037.1) a locally built release abi3 `.so` fails to load (LINKEDIT string-table offset misaligned by 4); agents worked around it with debug builds, and all local budget numbers for the Python path came from a separate release driver binary.

## Change
Add a pyarrow-free parity check (write tbl files, compare committed SHA-256 goldens) to the musl and Windows arm64 wheel jobs. Reproduce the macOS load failure, determine whether CI-built wheels load on macOS 27, and report to Apple or the Rust project as appropriate; add a wheel-load smoke test on the newest macOS runner available.

## Decision gates
- If CI-built wheels fail to load on macOS 27, raise priority to high and stop any cutover on macOS.
- Do not add linker workarounds (post-processing the .so) to release builds without owner approval.

## Guardrails
- BenchBox work only in a linked worktree (make worktree-create, make agent-write-preflight); the primary clone is read-only.
- Heavy work only through make heavy-run; never bypass or signal the lock, and never kill processes by name pattern (pkill -f); stop only PIDs you started.
- Commits as the configured human identity; no agent attribution.
- No carried or own reimplementation of upstream code without the owner decision recorded in datagen-decision-upstream-gap-policy.
- A choice between a small and a large implementation path goes to the owner with sizes before work starts.
- Report only results that were observed; name anything not run.
